articles.headline: Rams' Stafford passes Rivers for 6th all time in passing TDs
articles.description: Rams QB Matthew Stafford moved to sixth all-time in passing touchdowns after throwing his 426th to Davante Adams on Sunday night.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- With his third touchdown of the game Monday night, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford passed Philip Rivers for sole possession of sixth on the NFL's career passing touchdown list.

Stafford's third-quarter 11-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Davante Adams was his 426th career regular-season touchdown. He added another touchdown pass in the fourth quarter to give the Rams a 28-6 lead over the New York Giants.

Stafford now trails only Tom Brady (649), Drew Brees (571), Peyton Manning (539), Aaron Rodgers (528) and Brett Favre (508) on the all-time list.

Stafford finished the night 22 of 31 passing for 327 yards with four touchdowns and an interception in a win. 

Stafford is the second player in NFL history with 25 or more three-passing-touchdown games for multiple franchises (25 Rams, 42 Lions), according to ESPN Research. Manning had 64 with the Colts and 29 with the Broncos.

articles.headline: Giants QB Jaxson Dart exits MNF loss to Rams with knee injury
articles.description: Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart was ruled out for Monday night's game against the Rams after taking a hard hit on his left knee in the first quarter.
articles.body:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart left Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams after taking a hard hit on his left knee during his team's first series.

Dart went to the blue medical tent, where he was examined. He came out and walked with a limp to the locker room.

The team initially said he was questionable to return because of a knee injury but announced early in the third quarter that he would not return. 

"He's going to be OK," Giants general manager Joe Schoen told ESPN's Laura Rutledge.

Dart underwent X-rays at the stadium and later returned to the Giants' sideline in street clothes. 

Dart was hurt while being pressured on third-and-8. Rams linebacker Byron Young hit Dart from the quarterback's right side, sending him into linebacker Josaiah Stewart as he tried to tackle Dart, who landed hard on the turf. 

The second-year quarterback immediately grabbed at his left knee. He had completed 3 of 5 passes for 20 yards.

Jameis Winston replaced Dart at quarterback. Sources told ESPN that Dart tried to get back into the game in the first half, but the Giants wouldn't let him.

Winston started two games and appeared in three for the Giants in 2025, throwing for 567 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. The 11-year veteran was drafted No. 1 in 2015 and has also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, New Orleans Saints and Cleveland Browns.

Dart wasn't the only Giants star who left the game in the first half. Wide receiver Malik Nabers was hurt trying to make a catch in the second quarter.

Cornerback Trent McDuffie knocked down a pass intended for Nabers, who immediately grabbed at his right shoulder. Nabers went to the sideline and sank to the ground, where he was attended to by trainers for several minutes.

The third-year wide receiver, who came back last week from a torn ACL, then went to the bench and put a towel over his head. He was initially listed as questionable but returned to the field later in the second quarter.

Information from The Associated Press was included in this report.

articles.headline: Who has the most home runs for each MLB team all-time?
articles.description: Check out each team's all-time home run leaders.
articles.body:
No player in MLB history has hit more home runs for a single franchise than Hank Aaron, who launched 733 for the Braves. Every team has its own home run king and, as we progress through the 2026 season, a changing of the guard occurred in Kansas City.

On July 25, Salvador Perez climbed past George Brett on the Royals' all-time home run list after blasting his 318th career homer.

Below are each team's all-time home run leaders. Players in bold are still active on their respective teams.

Athletics - Mark McGwire, 363

articles.headline: Sources: Alec Pierce out weeks; Darius Slayton to join Colts
articles.description: Colts WR Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks because of a heel injury but will attempt to avoid surgery in the hopes of returning midseason.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Alec Pierce is expected to miss several weeks after aggravating a left heel injury in Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, and the team moved quickly to address his absence, agreeing to a deal with veteran Darius Slayton. 

Pierce will attempt to rehab the injury rather than have surgery, sources said, with the hope that he could return midseason. Surgery is still on the table, but that will depend on the success of the rehab. It's likely the wideout will be placed on injured reserve while he recovers.

The injury is to the same heel that Pierce had surgically repaired in March. His recovery from that procedure stretched longer than expected, with him missing training camp and returning to practice only last month. 

Pierce, who signed a four-year, $114 million contract in March, was expected to be a centerpiece of the Colts' offense this season. 

The Colts, already thin at receiver because of veteran backup Ashton Dulin's ankle injury, agreed to terms Monday night with Slayton, a free agent, sources told ESPN. A fellow member of the Giants' 2019 draft class, alongside current Colts quarterback Daniel Jones, Slayton caught 37 passes for 538 yards last season with New York, starting 12 games. 

The Colts' offense struggled to create explosive plays Sunday after Pierce's injury. But Slayton, even at 29, is seen as a player who could stretch the field. He has averaged a healthy 15 yards per catch in his career, including 14.5 last season.

So far, Jones has had difficulty replicating the explosiveness he had in the Colts' offense last season, when he averaged 8.1 yards per attempt. Through two games -- with Pierce limited in Week 1 and missing most of Sunday's game after his injury -- Jones has averaged 6.1 yards per attempt.

Slayton had his best seasons while playing alongside Jones in New York. In the four seasons he has played with Jones, at least in part, Slayton has surpassed 700 receiving yards.

ESPN's Stephen Holder contributed to this report.

articles.headline: River Ryan, key piece in Tarik Skubal deal, leads Tigers
articles.description: River Ryan, acquired from the Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, was outstanding in his Detroit debut Monday night, pitching three scoreless innings in a win against the Nationals.
articles.body:
DETROIT -- River Ryan was outstanding in his Detroit debut and the Tigers hit three home runs to rout the Washington Nationals 9-2 on Monday night, one day after being eliminated from the American League playoff race.

Ryan, acquired from the Los Angeles Dodgers in the Tarik Skubal trade, pitched three scoreless innings. ESPN's No. 51-ranked prospect allowed two hits and a walk with two strikeouts. Ryan is expected to start again in the season finale Sunday -- the day after Justin Verlander is scheduled to make his final major league start.

"I think with, kind of what I've been through this year with injuries and kind of being stuck behind a really elite rotation with the Dodgers, it was just great to be able to get out there and play ball at the big league level again," Ryan told reporters. 

Keider Montero (10-9) pitched four scoreless innings in relief of Ryan.

Washington starter DJ Herz (0-1) made his first big league appearance in nearly two years. Herz, who had Tommy John surgery in April 2025, pitched four innings, allowing four runs on five hits and two walks while striking out four.

The Tigers took a 2-0 lead in the first. Gleyber Torres walked, went to second on a wild pitch and scored on a ground-rule double from Hao-Yu Lee. After Herz got the first out, Eduardo Valencia singled to left field, with Lee scoring when James Wood misplayed the ball for an error.

Javier Baez made it 4-0 in the fourth, hitting his third homer of the season over the Tigers bullpen in left to bring home Dillon Dingler.

Detroit added five more runs in the fifth, three on Ben Malgeri's fourth homer and two on Spencer Torkelson's 25th.

That made it 9-0, but Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer to get the Nationals on the scoreboard in the eighth.

The Tigers announced before the game that, due to a bank merger, Comerica Park will be known as Fifth Third Park starting in 2027. That's the same name as the stadium for the Toledo Mud Hens, Detroit's Triple-A team.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Pete Alonso homers twice to reach 40 on the season, helps Orioles rally to 4-3 win over Blue Jays
articles.description: — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- — Pete Alonso homered twice, including a two-run shot in the eighth inning that lifted the Baltimore Orioles to a 4-3 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays on Monday night.


              The Orioles are on the verge of elimination in the American League wild-card race, but Alonso has been terrific in his first season with the team. He has 40 home runs — the fourth time he's reached that mark in a season — and he's opened a nine-RBI lead on Triple Crown hopeful Yordan Alvarez of Houston.


              In fact, Alonso might be the one who ends up leading the AL in homers and RBI. He's one home run behind Tampa Bay slugger Junior Caminero.


              The Blue Jays brought in submarine right-hander Tyler Rogers (2-3) to face Alonso, who became just the second right-handed hitter to homer off him over the last two seasons.


              Yennier Cano (4-3) won in relief for the Orioles, and Rico Garcia worked a perfect ninth for his 10th save.


              Nathan Lukes and George Springer hit RBI singles during Toronto's three-run first inning, but the Blue Jays fell 3 1/2 games behind the idle Chicago White Sox for the final wild card in the AL.


              Trey Yesavage returned to the mound for the Blue Jays after knee inflammation sent him to the injured list in early August. He pitched only two innings, allowing a home run to Alonso in the first.


              Gunnar Henderson homered in the sixth for the Orioles and finished a double shy of the cycle.


              After the start was delayed 47 minutes because of rain, the first four Toronto batters reached base. Shane Baz was called for a pitch-clock violation with the count full to Brett Bateman. Then he issued another walk to Alejandro Kirk on a debatable checked-swing call.


              Lukes and Springer followed with hits to make it 2-0. A sacrifice fly by Sean Keys brought home another run.


              Baz held Toronto scoreless after that and made it through 6 2/3 innings.


              Bateman left the game with a hip injury after making a sliding catch in center field in the second. X-rays were negative.


              Up next
              Blue Jays RHP Max Scherzer (3-8) starts Tuesday night against Chris Bassitt (8-5) of the Orioles.


              ------
